notes.title: It Takes a Village Monthly Devlog Update - July
notes.content:
Hey everyone, hope you are off to a lovely summer so far.  Over here at Hoftware.io, we are working hard to continue to iterate on It Takes a Village and provide better and polished gameplay mechanics to the game.  Its been a while since we've had a proper update, so lets dive right in to the new features that I've been working on the last months.


[h2]Forest Biome[/h2]
As a villager, you're going to want to build your village.  To do so, you're going to need some new resources and recipes in order to do that and to progress in the game.  Over the last two months, I've been planning and building out the first biome/level that you will take on in the game.  In the image above you can see my crude attempt at level design.  It reminded me of all the game manuals I used to buy for each of the GameBoy Pokemon games.  Once I had this plan in place, I was able to implement it in the game world.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44921856/c03662719b22960cbba067fa9d17752eb5fb4dda.png[/img]

[h2]Archery[/h2]
I wanted to add some variety to the types of combat you can play around with in-game.  I also want to add some variety to the puzzles that I'll put in to the game that will utilize combat in nuanced ways.  This is where archery comes in.  I've tried to implement it similar to how you'd expect in old-school Zelda games.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44921856/7f44fe6bc3040cc74060dd102ed2dc2e366932de.gif[/img]

[h2]Quest System[/h2]
No RPG is complete without a quest system.  And mine is no different.  But, I did take the liberty of gutting the idea of a quest system down to the basic level.  This is partially for saving myself work and complexity down the line and partially for me actually wanting to release this game at some point.  With that said, I was able to add villagers who can trigger quests, give you specific items, and trigger world events.  This was the last system I needed for the base demo to be complete!  This is a huge milestone as it means I can focus now on smashing bugs and making the game as fun as I can instead of working on the core systems.

[h2]The Demo[/h2]
Now, we are full steam ahead towards getting a demo out so that you guys can go ahead and play the game.  I'm hoping to have this ready in the next two months.  I set a goal for the end of summer to have a demo ready to go.  

Thank you so much for your support so far!  I'm grateful for those of you who are interested in my small project.  It means the world to me.  

I've started a Twitter account where I'm posting more regular feedback.  If you're interested in following along more intently, give me a follow and feel free to reach out with more personal feedback!

https://x.com/Hoftware


Thanks,
Brandon | Hoftware.io

notes.title: It Takes a Village Monthly Devlog Update - April
notes.content:
Hey everyone, its been a month since my last update for It Takes a Village so I thought I'd take some time to fill you in on what's been going in the dev cave these last weeks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44921856/e6d02aa73c12e21297a05aa46b8a3b793ee504eb.png[/img]

[h2]Village Life[/h2]
The main focus has been primarily focused around village life and making it as engaging as possible.  I've added a basic dialog system for the villagers to give them a bit more personality and not leave them like the soulless workers they previous were.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44921856/f545bfd5b3b4496cf1ca0484f117a156118854c5.png[/img]

[h2]New Enemies[/h2]
Every good game needs expressive and interesting enemies to fight.  It Takes a Village is no different.  Last week I added a Cyclops enemy to be the first real test you will face as a hero in training.  It has a range of AoE and ranged attacks to choose from based on its current situation.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44921856/23bfe1e7baa425a01e13b9316351d57ad4276eb3.png[/img]

[h2]Placement System[/h2]
I've revamped the icons that will represent the different items you can place within the game.  This was to give a fresh coat of paint to the rather gross placeholder icons I had previously.  This should give a much more professional look and match the aesthetic of the game.

[h2]Next Steps[/h2]
All of this work is looking towards releasing a full trailer for the game to really show off what a player can expect from the game.  Static images and gifs are one thing, but being able to see prolonged gameplay and finalizing the game loop is a much more difficult thing to achieve.  I hope to have this ready in the next 2-3 weeks.  I'll announce it to you all once its ready for viewing so stay tuned!

Thank you so much for your support so far in It Takes a Village's development, and I will speak to you soon!

notes.title: Hello World!
notes.content:
Hello World!  

This is the first of many devlogs to come as I continue to develop It Takes a Village.  If you are reading this, let me first thank you for your support from the bottom of my heart.  Its always been a dream of mine to be able to create on a game for people to enjoy and I hope you find that in It Takes a Village.

For this first devlog, I thought it'd be good to give a bit of context on the project and myself as I develop the game.  First off, my name is Brandon, and I live in London, UK working full time at a fin-tech in town.  I work on It Takes a Village in my free time, and I have been working on the project since I got married last July.  I am a solo developer who has worked on the modeling, coding, and marketing for this project.  With all of these hats, patience is a virtue in seeing progress with this game.  

But what is "It Takes a Village" [i]really[/i]?  Well, its really a love letter to my childhood.  I remember growing up and getting my first Game Boy.  My family was moving from one state to another and to smooth over the whole uprooting my social circle as a fragile Kindergardener, my parents got me a Game Boy and Pokemon Yellow.  Ever since then, I've been fascinated by games and the impact they can have on people.  30 years and a Computer Science degree later, I too wanted to be able to have that same kind of impact upon others through my own works and ideas.  This is where It Takes a Village starts.

My two favorite games growing up were Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons and Animal Crossing.  One allowed you to be the hero you aspired to be in real life.  You fought through hordes of baddies and had to solve some pretty intricate puzzles.  The other allowed you to slow down and play a more comfortable game.  Make your house your own.  Pay off that greedy Tom Nook at your own pace.  Build a community that you could be proud of and show off to your friends.  I wanted to create a game that blended these two elements and could tell a story in the process.

Now when I created the notion page and spec'ed out the feature list for these things, I realized that's quite a big endeavor to take on.  Something the industry calls "feature creep."  This was not going to be an easy project nor was I immune to the likely scenario that I would lose focus and ultimately give up on the project altogether.  Regardless, I put in a few safeguards to prevent this sort of burn out and began work on the project.  

Since I started the project in July, I have charted my work and laid out the systems needed for the game.  You can see my current progress here:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44921856/fe18d1e78f85a7942c79ce8c7c2afb9469d56820.png[/img]

In future devlogs, I'll go into how I chart this progress, but its safe to say I've got around 60% of the major systems completed and about 15% of the content done.  Its a weird split, but I reckon it works quite well.  For example, I've completed the base inventory system for the game so you as a player can equip, use, and store any item you find in the game.  This is 100% complete from a [i]coding [/i]perspective.  But, I only have a few items that I've used for testing in game.  There are many many more that still needed to be added, but I can add these once I've finished the foundation for the game.  This is 5% complete from a [i]content [/i]perspective.  

Over the next weeks, I'll be keeping you up to date on the progress of the game and the work that I am currently doing.  It may be a bit slow as my wife and I are enjoying some much needed rest in Thailand at the moment, but once I get back home, I plan to continue to flesh out the combat system for the game.  At the moment, I can get Villagers to attack Bandits and Bandits to attack Villagers and the player, but its still clunky at best.  

If you've made it this far, thank you so much for reading and for being interested in my game.  I hope to reach as many people as I can, but I am thankful for everyone who has thus far climbed onboard for the ride.  Thank you for your support and see you soon!

Brandon
